papers.title: CtBP1/2 restrict DUX-dependent and independent 2C-like programs in mouse embryonic stem cells.
papers.authors: Yoshioka K, Ichisakino M, Sugiyama K, Hayakawa N, Abadi SA, Yoon H, Marutani M, Masuda R, Takahashi K, Seki Y.
papers.abstract: After fertilization, maternally deposited mRNAs are cleared, and de novo transcription is initiated through zygotic genome activation (ZGA), a core event of the maternal-to-zygotic transition in mice. 2-cell-like cells (2CLCs), a rare MERVL-positive subpopulation of mouse embryonic stem cells, partially recapitulate transcriptional features of 2-cell embryos. Although canonical MERVL-high 2CLCs depend on DUX, Dux knockout embryos can develop to term, suggesting that 2CLC models do not fully capture DUX-independent pathways associated with preimplantation transcriptional programs. Here, we show that disruption of C-terminal binding protein 1/2 (Ctbp1/2) activates both DUX-dependent minor ZGA-associated genes and DUX-independent major ZGA- and post-ZGA-associated programs. Pramel7 is derepressed independently of DUX and contributes to subsets of both programs. PRAMEL7 overexpression partially rescues transcriptional defects caused by Dux deletion and is associated with UHRF1 downregulation and DNA demethylation-linked activation of post-ZGA-associated genes. These findings identify CtBP1/2 as repressors of multiple early embryonic transcriptional programs in mouse embryonic stem cells.

papers.title: PAIP1 couples mRNA export to cytoplasmic mRNP remodeling and poly(A) homeostasis
papers.authors: Overwijn D, Dörner K, de Almeida C, Müller M, Mironov A, Ivanek R, Skrinjar P, Gut MJ, Solheim I, Beuret N, Bock T, Zeug M, Smialek M, Brandkamp S, Maier T, Zavolan M, Keller Valsecchi CI, Hondele M.
papers.abstract: SUMMARY Messenger ribonucleoproteins (mRNPs) acquire distinct protein compositions as they move from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, yet how this transition is coordinated and how inefficient remodeling affects downstream mRNA metabolism remains poorly understood. Here, we identify PAIP1 as a metazoan cofactor of the mRNA export ATPase DDX19. By binding a conserved N-terminal motif in DDX19, PAIP1 is recruited to the nuclear pore, where it promotes exchange of the nuclear poly(A)-binding protein PABPN1 for cytoplasmic PABPC1, thereby coupling mRNA export to cytoplasmic mRNP maturation. PAIP1 depletion alters cytoplasmic mRNP composition, mRNA stability and poly(A)-tail homeostasis. In Drosophila embryos, where poly(A)-tail regulation of maternal mRNAs directs early development, maternal PAIP1 depletion shortens poly(A)-tails, delays zygotic genome activation, and causes severe developmental defects. Our findings identify an export-coupled mRNP maturation pathway linking PABP exchange to downstream mRNA metabolism.

papers.title: Transcriptomic view of key events during early embryogenesis in the duplicated Atlantic salmon genome
papers.authors: Sharma Humagain P, Perojil Morata D, Wessel MI, Seilo Torgersen J, Lien S, Kent MP, Macqueen D, Boyartchuk V.
papers.abstract: Early embryogenesis is governed by tightly regulated transcriptional programs, including the maternal-to-zygotic transition (MZT), zygotic genome activation (ZGA), and maintenance of pluripotency. While these processes are well studied in model vertebrates, they remain poorly understood in salmonid fishes, whose genomes are shaped by a relatively recent whole genome duplication (WGD) event. Here, we present a temporally resolved transcriptomic analysis of Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) embryogenesis using bulk RNA-seq across key stages spanning early embryogenesis. Dimensionality reduction and unsupervised clustering of gene expression revealed stage-specific transitions encompassing maternal RNA clearance, cell cycle regulation, and the onset of metabolic activity. We demonstrate that ZGA occurs early and in multiple phases, beginning soon after fertilization, accompanied by chromatin remodelling and the activation of epigenetic regulators. Duplicated gene pairs retained from the salmonid WGD frequently displayed asynchronous expression, indicative of functional divergence and the evolution of additional regulatory complexity of embryonic development. To gain insights into pluripotency, we integrated analyses of gene expression, transcription factor motifs, and chromatin accessibility, to reveal conserved regulators including genes encoding Pou5f3, Nanog, and Sox19b, alongside divergent functions of Klf family members. Our cross-stage profiling allowed us to define a novel panel of stably-expressed reference genes for normalization during quantitative PCR analyses, which were used to validate pluripotency- and differentiation-associated dynamics inferred by RNA-seq. Together, our findings delineate the transcriptional architecture of early embryogenesis in Atlantic salmon, revealing both conserved and lineage-specific features of pluripotency regulation, and providing a foundational resource for future functional genomics and stem cell applications in salmonids.

papers.title: The role of transposable elements-endogenous retroviruses in embryonic development and regeneration.
papers.authors: Li Z, Huang Y, Ju Z, Le R, Chen Z.
papers.abstract: Endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) are dynamically regulated across the lifespan and can function as context-dependent components of host gene-regulatory networks. During embryonic development, selected ERV-derived elements are co-opted to support zygotic genome activation, lineage specification, and placental development. In adult tissues, ERV-derived sequences can contribute to tissue and immune homeostasis, whereas potentially disruptive ERV activity is constrained by epigenetic mechanisms. During regeneration and somatic cell reprogramming, ERV and broader transposable-element programs undergo transient, locus-specific remodeling. In aging, the weakening of epigenetic and nuclear restraint can promote aberrant ERV derepression, inflammation, and functional decline. This review summarizes the diverse roles of ERVs across these contexts and discusses the challenges of defining locus-specific functions, resolving repetitive sequences, and developing safe ERV-targeted interventions.

papers.title: Asymmetric chromatin accessibility underlies anterior-posterior axis specification in moth fly embryos.
papers.authors: Amiri EE, Li M, Tenger-Trolander A, Devine M, Julian AT, Kasan K, Sanders SA, Blythe SA, Schmidt-Ott U.
papers.abstract: Establishing the anterior-posterior (AP) body axis is a fundamental process during embryogenesis, and the fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster, provides one of the best-known case studies. But for unknown reasons, different species of flies (Diptera) establish the AP axis through unrelated, structurally distinct anterior determinants. The anterior determinant of Drosophila, Bicoid (Bcd), initiates symmetry-breaking during nuclear cleavage cycles (NCs) when ubiquitous pioneer factors, such as Zelda (Zld), drive zygotic genome activation (ZGA) at the level of chromatin accessibility by nucleosome depletion. While Bcd engages in a concentration-dependent competition with nucleosomes at the loci of a small set of transcription factor (TF) genes that are expressed in the anterior embryo, it remains unknown whether unrelated anterior determinants of other fly species function in the same way and target homologous genes. We have examined the symmetry-breaking mechanism of a moth fly, Clogmia albipunctata, in which a maternally expressed transcript isoform of the pair-rule segmentation gene odd-paired serves as an anterior determinant. We provide a de novo assembly and annotation of the Clogmia genome, report changes in chromatin accessibility during the nuclear cleavage cycles (NCs) of consecutive blastoderm stages, and describe how Clogmia's orthologs of zelda (Cal-zld) and odd-paired (Cal-opa) affect chromatin accessibility and gene expression. We document extensive opening and closing of chromatin regions during cleavage cycles of blastoderm, important roles of Cal-zld in opening chromatin and driving zygotic gene expression, and show that maternal Cal-opa activity initiates zygotic symmetry-breaking along the AP axis by driving chromatin accessibility and expression at Clogmia's homeobrain and sloppy-paired loci. These genes are not known as key targets of Bcd but may serve a more widely conserved role in the initiation of anterior pattern formation, given their early anterior expression and function in head development in insects.

papers.importance_implication: This reveals a conserved mechanism for AP axis specification across Diptera, where maternal odd-paired isoforms act as anterior determinants without Bcd, challenging the assumption that Bcd is the universal anterior determinant in flies.

papers.title: High-resolution mapping of embryonic genome activation unveils a decoupling of transcription activation from precocious H3K4me3 removal.
papers.authors: Al-Mousawi J, Michetti L, Castaldi L, Liu N, Villacorta L, Benes V, Boskovic A.
papers.abstract: The lack of temporal resolution in transcriptomic data during mammalian embryonic genome activation (EGA) has precluded the comprehensive understanding of the functional relationships between the various gene regulatory mechanisms governing this process. Here, we finely dissect the transcriptional dynamics of mouse EGA using precision in vitro fertilization (IVF) coupled with single-embryo RNA sequencing. Our highly temporally resolved dataset uncovers an extensive, step-wise remodeling of the embryonic messenger RNA landscape, affecting ∼30% of the total detectable transcripts over a 9-hour time frame. We capture the gradual shift from maternal to embryonic messenger RNAs, successfully identify ribosome biogenesis and translation as hallmarks of EGA, and find previously unidentified gene expression dynamics. We further uncover a set of eight histone demethylating enzymes among the earliest up-regulated EGA genes and leverage our precision-IVF to dissect the transcriptional versus developmental impact of histone H3 lysine-4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) remodeling after fertilization. Our results indicate that precocious removal of H3K4me3 from embryonic chromatin only modestly affects embryonic transcription without perturbing EGA timing, arguing against a major instructive role of precocious remodeling of maternally inherited H3K4me3 after fertilization on genome activation. High-resolution transcriptome mapping coupled with functional perturbations allows us to distinguish direct gene expression effects from general impacts on developmental timing, opening avenues for further quantitative characterization of the impact of epigenome remodeling on embryonic transcription.

papers.importance_implication: This work provides critical temporal resolution for understanding the functional relationships between gene regulatory mechanisms during EGA, distinguishing direct transcriptional effects from developmental timing impacts of epigenome remodeling, which has implications for understanding the role of maternal-to-zygotic transitions in early development.

grant_ideas.rationale: The current study shows minimal impact of H3K4me3 removal on transcription in mice; Xenopus laevis has a more rapid ZGA with distinct maternal-to-zygotic transitions, making it a model to test if H3K4me3 removal timing is critical for ZGA initiation.

grant_ideas.hypothesis: The eight histone demethylases identified as early EGA genes in mice are functionally conserved in Xenopus laevis and regulate ZGA through precise removal of H3K4me3 at the 2-cell stage.
grant_ideas.rationale: The study identifies eight histone demethylases among earliest up-regulated EGA genes in mice; Xenopus has a rapid ZGA with similar epigenetic dynamics, allowing testing of conserved roles in ZGA initiation.
grant_ideas.design: Perform single-embryo epigenomic profiling (H3K4me3 ChIP-seq) at 2-cell stage in Xenopus embryos with and without targeted inhibition of specific histone demethylases (e.g., KDM5A) using CRISPRi.
grant_ideas.readouts_controls: Primary readout: H3K4me3 levels at ZGA genes; Controls: Unperturbed embryos, embryos with non-targeted CRISPRi, embryos with H3K4me3 demethylase inhibitors.
grant_ideas.support_refute: Supporting result: If specific demethylases reduce H3K4me3 at ZGA genes, it confirms their role in ZGA. Refuting result: If H3K4me3 levels remain unchanged despite inhibition, it suggests redundancy or alternative mechanisms.
grant_ideas.novelty_feasibility_risk: Novelty: First study to link specific histone demethylases to ZGA in Xenopus. Feasibility: Xenopus has established CRISPRi tools and epigenomic profiling. Risk: Demethylases may have non-epigenetic roles in Xenopus development.

grant_ideas.title: Impact of maternal H3K4me3 persistence on Xenopus ZGA timing
grant_ideas.hypothesis: Maternal H3K4me3 persistence in Xenopus embryos beyond the 2-cell stage delays ZGA initiation without affecting transcriptional output.
grant_ideas.rationale: The study shows that precocious H3K4me3 removal in mice has minimal impact on EGA timing; Xenopus has a more rapid ZGA, so maternal H3K4me3 persistence may have a more pronounced effect on timing.
grant_ideas.design: Use maternal H3K4me3 enrichment via CRISPR-based epigenetic editing at 1-cell stage in Xenopus embryos, followed by live imaging of ZGA timing (e.g., Xbra expression) and single-embryo RNA-seq at 2-4 cell stages.
grant_ideas.readouts_controls: Primary readout: ZGA timing (onset of Xbra expression); Controls: Unperturbed embryos, embryos with H3K4me3 enrichment, embryos with H3K4me3 removal inhibitors.
grant_ideas.support_refute: Supporting result: If maternal H3K4me3 persistence delays ZGA, it suggests a role in timing. Refuting result: If ZGA timing is unaffected, it implies maternal H3K4me3 is not rate-limiting.
grant_ideas.novelty_feasibility_risk: Novelty: First study to test maternal H3K4me3 persistence in Xenopus ZGA. Feasibility: Xenopus has well-established ZGA timing assays. Risk: H3K4me3 may be rapidly remodeled in Xenopus embryos.

ranked_grant_directions.title: ERV-driven zygotic genome activation in early Xenopus laevis embryos
ranked_grant_directions.rationale: Xenopus laevis is a model with well-characterized ZGA dynamics; ERVs are co-opted for ZGA in multiple species, and CRISPR deletion of specific ERV elements can directly test necessity without cross-species conservation concerns.
ranked_grant_directions.significance: High: Directly addresses a key question in ZGA initiation with potential to reveal ERV roles in maternal-to-zygotic transition.
ranked_grant_directions.novelty: High: First direct test of ERV necessity in Xenopus ZGA; existing literature focuses on mammals and Drosophila.
ranked_grant_directions.feasibility: High: Xenopus ZGA is well-studied with established tools for CRISPR and RNA-seq.
ranked_grant_directions.risk: Moderate: Potential off-target effects from CRISPR; requires careful validation with non-ERV controls.

ranked_grant_directions.title: Impact of PAIP1 on maternal mRNA stability during Xenopus MZT
ranked_grant_directions.rationale: PAIP1 links mRNA export to poly(A)-tail homeostasis, and its depletion in Drosophila delays ZGA; Xenopus has rapid maternal mRNA turnover during MZT, making it ideal for testing.
ranked_grant_directions.significance: High: Maternal mRNA stability is a critical bottleneck in MZT; understanding PAIP1's role could reveal conserved mechanisms for mRNA regulation.
ranked_grant_directions.novelty: Medium: First study to link PAIP1 to maternal mRNA stability in Xenopus MZT; PAIP1 has been studied in Drosophila but not in Xenopus.
ranked_grant_directions.feasibility: High: Xenopus has established RNA-seq protocols and siRNA knockdown tools for early embryos.
ranked_grant_directions.risk: Moderate: Technical challenges in RNA-seq at early stages; requires multiple controls to ensure specificity.

ranked_grant_directions.title: Temporal dynamics of H3K4me3 removal during Xenopus laevis early development
ranked_grant_directions.rationale: The mouse study shows minimal impact of H3K4me3 removal on EGA timing; Xenopus has a more rapid ZGA, so maternal H3K4me3 persistence may have a pronounced effect on timing.
ranked_grant_directions.significance: Medium: H3K4me3 dynamics are a key epigenetic regulator of ZGA; Xenopus offers a model to test if maternal H3K4me3 persistence delays ZGA.
ranked_grant_directions.novelty: Medium: First study to test H3K4me3 removal timing in Xenopus ZGA; similar studies exist in mice but not in Xenopus.
ranked_grant_directions.feasibility: High: Xenopus has well-established IVF protocols and CRISPR tools for epigenetic editing.
ranked_grant_directions.risk: Moderate: H3K4me3 may be rapidly remodeled in Xenopus embryos, masking effects of perturbation.

ranked_grant_directions.title: ERV-mediated lineage specification in early Xenopus laevis embryos
ranked_grant_directions.rationale: ERVs are co-opted for lineage specification in multiple species; Xenopus has well-defined mesoderm markers, allowing testing of ERV roles in mesoderm formation.
ranked_grant_directions.significance: Medium: Lineage specification is a critical step in early development; ERVs could play a conserved role in mesoderm formation.
ranked_grant_directions.novelty: Medium: First test of ERVs in Xenopus mesoderm specification; ERVs have been studied in mammals but not in Xenopus lineage specification.
ranked_grant_directions.feasibility: Moderate: Xenopus lineage tracing is established, but requires precise timing of CRISPR disruption.
ranked_grant_directions.risk: Moderate: Potential developmental compensation by alternative pathways; ERVs may not be critical for mesoderm formation.

synthesis.why_xenopus_now: Xenopus laevis provides a unique combination of rapid ZGA, well-characterized maternal-to-zygotic transitions, and externally accessible early developmental stages, making it ideal for testing conserved mechanisms of ZGA and MZT with minimal technical barriers compared to mammalian models.
